places.name: Tashkent
places.summary: Uzbekistan's capital and main international gateway, a big, green Soviet-planned city of wide avenues, fountains and metro palaces, with an older Muslim quarter around Chorsu. Worth a day or two for its bazaar, museums and the Hazrati Imam complex before heading west.
facts: Main arrival hub; Afrosiyob trains to Samarkand and Bukhara leave from Tashkent Central (Tashkent Vokzal) station
Use Yandex Go for cheap taxis (most rides ~20,000–40,000 UZS)
Many museums close one day a week (often Monday) – check before going
places.season: Hot summers (35 °C+ in July–August); April–May and September–October are ideal.

places.name: Hazrati Imam (Khast Imam) Complex
places.summary: Tashkent's religious centre in the old town: the Barak Khan Madrasa, Tilla Sheikh and Hazrati Imam mosques and the Muyi Mubarak library. The library holds the Uthman Qur'an, one of the oldest surviving Qur'an manuscripts.
facts: Courtyard free; small fee (~30,000–50,000 UZS) for the Qur'an library
Modest dress: cover shoulders and knees, women bring a headscarf for the mosques
Combine with Chorsu Bazaar and Kukeldash Madrasa (2 km)

places.name: Chorsu Bazaar
places.summary: Tashkent's great old-town market under a turquoise dome, with spices, dried fruit, nuts, bread, and a huge meat and dairy hall. The surrounding stalls sell textiles, skullcaps and ceramics.
facts: Free; open daily from early morning, busiest and liveliest in the morning
Chorsu metro station is right next to it
Watch your pockets in the crowds; bargain for souvenirs

places.name: Kukeldash Madrasa
places.summary: Large 16th-century madrasa on a rise beside Chorsu Bazaar, one of the few pre-Russian buildings to survive in Tashkent. Still a working religious school, with a modest courtyard and craft stalls.
facts: Small entry fee (~10,000–20,000 UZS)
Two minutes' walk from Chorsu Bazaar
Modest dress

places.name: Tashkent Metro stations
places.summary: Soviet-era metro with lavishly decorated stations – chandeliers, marble and themed mosaics, best at Kosmonavtlar, Alisher Navoi and Tashkent stations. Photography is now allowed, making a short metro hop a sight in itself.
facts: Fare ~2,000–3,000 UZS per ride (pay by card or ATTO transport card/QR)
Ride a few stops on the blue (Uzbekistan) and red (Chilonzor) lines
Avoid the 08:00–09:00 and 17:00–19:00 rush

places.name: Amir Timur Museum
places.summary: Blue-domed museum beside Amir Timur Square dedicated to Timur (Tamerlane) and the Timurid dynasty, with a gilded interior, manuscripts, weapons and models of Timurid monuments. A good primer before Samarkand and Shahrisabz.
facts: Ticket ~30,000–40,000 UZS; photo permit extra
About 1 hour
Right next to Amir Timur Square and the Hotel Uzbekistan

places.name: State Museum of History of Uzbekistan
places.wiki: State Museum of History of Uzbekistan
places.summary: The country's main history museum, from Stone Age finds and Buddhist art from Termez (including the Fayaz Tepe Buddha triad) to the Silk Road and the Soviet era. Gives useful context for the whole trip.
facts: Allow 1–1.5 hours
Short walk from Independence Square

places.name: State Museum of Applied Arts
places.wiki: State Museum of Applied Arts of Uzbekistan
places.summary: Housed in a 19th-century Russian diplomat's mansion decorated by craftsmen with carved ganch, painted wood and tilework. The collection of suzani embroidery, ceramics, jewellery and textiles is the best overview of Uzbek crafts.
facts: The building's interiors are as much the attraction as the exhibits
Small shop with good-quality crafts

places.name: Independence Square (Mustaqillik Maydoni)
places.summary: Tashkent's vast ceremonial square with government buildings, fountains, the stork-topped arch and the Monument of Independence. Pleasant for an evening stroll.
facts: Free
Combine with the State History Museum next door
Some areas around government buildings are fenced off

places.name: Navoi Opera and Ballet Theatre
places.summary: Grand 1947 theatre whose six side foyers are each decorated in the style of a different Uzbek region. Opera and ballet tickets are inexpensive, making an evening performance an easy treat.
facts: Tickets usually ~50,000–200,000 UZS; buy at the box office or online
Performances most evenings except in the summer break
Smart-casual dress

places.name: Tashkent TV Tower
places.summary: 375 m television tower, the tallest structure in Central Asia, with an observation deck at about 100 m and a revolving restaurant. Good views over the flat city to the mountains on clear days.
facts: Ticket for the observation deck ~50,000–100,000 UZS for foreigners; bring your passport
Security check at the entrance
Clearest views after rain or in autumn/winter

places.name: Zangi Ata Mausoleum
places.summary: Timurid-era shrine complex of the Sufi saint Zangi Ata in the town of Zangiota just south-west of Tashkent, with a tiled portal, mosque and peaceful courtyard. A pilgrimage site still busy with local visitors.
facts: Free (donations welcome)
About 30 minutes by taxi from central Tashkent
Modest dress; women should cover their hair

places.name: Chimgan
places.summary: Small mountain resort area in the western Tian Shan about 1.5 hours from Tashkent, with chairlifts, guesthouses and trails at the foot of Greater Chimgan. Locals come in summer to escape the heat and in winter to ski.
facts: Day trip or overnight from Tashkent by taxi (~85 km)
Chairlift rides ~50,000–100,000 UZS
Weekends are busy with Tashkent families
places.season: Ski season December–March; hiking best May–October.

places.name: Greater Chimgan summit hike
places.summary: Full-day climb to the 3,309 m summit of Greater Chimgan, the highest peak near Tashkent, with views over the Charvak Reservoir and the Ugam and Pskem ranges. Steep and rocky in its upper part.
facts: 8–10 hours return from Chimgan, ~1,700 m of ascent
Start very early and carry plenty of water; no water on the upper slopes
A local guide is recommended
places.caution: Upper slopes are steep scree; avoid in snow or bad weather without a guide.
places.season: Best June–September once the snow has gone.

places.name: Beldersay chairlift
places.summary: Long chairlift rising to around 2,000 m on the Kumbel ridge above Beldersay, with wide views over the Chimgan massif and towards Charvak. In winter it serves freeride skiers.
facts: Lift ticket ~100,000 UZS return (approx.)
Bring a warm layer – it is much colder at the top
Lifts may stop in high wind

places.name: Amirsoy Mountain Resort
places.summary: Modern ski and all-season resort opened in 2019 with gondolas, chairlifts and restaurants, the most polished mountain facility in Uzbekistan. In summer the gondola gives easy access to alpine meadows and views.
facts: Gondola tickets sold online and at the base; prices vary by season
About 1.5 hours from Tashkent
Book accommodation well ahead in ski season

places.name: Gulkam Gorge
places.summary: Narrow canyon east of Chimgan with a series of small waterfalls, cascades and pools; the classic adventurous day hike in the area. The lower section is a scramble along the stream with some fixed ropes.
facts: 4–6 hours return; wear shoes with good grip that can get wet
Go with a guide if you're not used to scrambling
Avoid after heavy rain
places.caution: Slippery rocks and a few exposed scrambles; not for small children.

places.name: Charvak Reservoir
places.summary: Large turquoise reservoir framed by mountains, Tashkent's summer playground with beaches, boat trips and resorts on its shores. Worth a stop for the views from the dam and the coast road towards Brichmulla.
facts: Beaches and lake resorts charge entry; some free spots along the shore
Swimming season June–September
Weekend traffic from Tashkent can be heavy

places.name: Brichmulla (Burchmullo)
places.summary: Mountain village at the eastern tip of Charvak, where the Chatkal and Koksu valleys meet, famous in Uzbekistan from a popular song. A base for walks and the drive along the Chatkal river.
facts: Simple guesthouses and resorts
Good starting point for Ugam-Chatkal National Park walks
Fresh trout restaurants along the river

places.name: Khumsan
places.summary: Village in the Ugam valley north of Charvak with orchards, small resorts and trails into the Ugam range. Quieter than Chimgan.
facts: Guesthouses and summer camps
Trails up side valleys; a guide helps with route-finding
Cooler than Tashkent in summer

places.name: Ugam-Chatkal National Park
places.summary: Large protected area of the western Tian Shan covering the Ugam, Pskem and Chatkal ranges, with juniper forests, walnut groves, rivers and wildlife such as ibex. Day hikes from Brichmulla and Khumsan.
facts: Some valleys near the Kyrgyz/Kazakh border need a permit – go with a local agency
Best visited with a guide
Bring water and sun protection
places.season: Late spring flowers in May–June; autumn colours in October.

places.name: Pskem River gorge
places.summary: Wild river gorge entering Charvak from the north-east, with steep walls and views up the Pskem valley. The lower part is a scenic drive from the reservoir.
facts: Upper Pskem valley is a border zone requiring a permit
Rafting trips run in early summer
Combine with Charvak and Brichmulla

places.name: Kokand
places.summary: Former capital of the Kokand Khanate and first stop in the Fergana Valley on the road or train from Tashkent. Known for Khudayar Khan's palace, wooden-columned mosques and old madrasas.
facts: Train from Tashkent (~4–5 h) or shared taxi over the Kamchik Pass
Half a day covers the main sights
Good hotel options for a first valley night

places.name: Palace of Khudayar Khan
places.summary: Brightly tiled 1870s palace of the last Kokand khan, with a long arcaded facade, courtyards and painted ceilings, now a museum. The finest building in the Fergana Valley.
facts: About 1 hour
Best light on the facade in the afternoon

places.name: Fergana
places.summary: Leafy Russian-built regional capital with tree-lined avenues, parks and the valley's best range of hotels. A convenient base for Margilan, Rishtan and Kuva.
facts: Airport and train station with links to Tashkent
Margilan's silk workshops are 20 minutes away
Pleasant evening walks in the central park

places.name: Margilan
places.summary: Ancient Silk Road town and centre of Uzbek silk weaving, famous for its ikat (atlas and adras) fabrics. Workshops, a lively bazaar and old mosques make it the valley's most rewarding stop.
facts: Combine the Yodgorlik silk factory with Kumtepa bazaar
Craft workshops welcome visitors; buy ikat directly from weavers
Guesthouses available, or stay in Fergana

places.name: Yodgorlik Silk Factory
places.summary: Working silk factory where you see the whole process by hand: boiling cocoons, reeling silk, dyeing threads in ikat patterns and weaving on traditional looms. One of the best craft visits in Central Asia.
facts: Free or small fee for a guided tour; English-speaking guides often available
Open weekdays and Saturday mornings; weaving stops on Sundays
Shop sells silk at fair, fixed prices

places.name: Kumtepa Bazaar
places.summary: Traditional village market outside Margilan where locals in skullcaps and atlas dresses trade fabric, livestock and household goods. Busy and atmospheric on market days.
facts: Main market days Thursday and Sunday, mornings are best
Good place to buy ikat at local prices
Ask before photographing people

places.name: Rishtan
places.summary: Town famous for centuries for its blue-and-green ishkor-glazed ceramics, made from local red clay. Master potters such as Rustam Usmanov open their workshops to visitors.
facts: Workshop visits free; pieces from ~50,000 UZS
On the road between Kokand and Fergana
Ceramics can be wrapped for travel

places.name: Kuva Buddhist temple ruins
places.summary: Remains of an early medieval town with a Buddhist sanctuary in Kuva, east of Fergana, where large clay Buddha statues were excavated. A small park-like archaeological site.
facts: Small fee or free
30–40 minutes from Fergana
Only foundations remain; for archaeology fans

places.name: Andijan
places.summary: Eastern valley city and birthplace of Babur, founder of the Mughal empire, with the Babur literary museum and a big Jami Mosque complex. Gateway to the Kyrgyz border at Dostyk/Osh.
facts: Babur museum in his reconstructed house
Large bazaar near the Jami Mosque
Train link to Tashkent

places.name: Namangan
places.summary: Large, conservative city in the north of the valley, known for its flower festival, the Mullah Kyrgyz madrasa and fine parks. Few foreign visitors.
facts: Base for Akhsikath and Chust
Flower festival in May
Dress conservatively

places.name: Akhsikath
places.summary: Earthen ruins of the medieval capital of Fergana on a bluff above the Syr Darya, mentioned by Babur. Wide river views and excavated walls.
facts: Free or small fee
About 30 minutes from Namangan
Shadeless; go early or late in summer

places.name: Chust
places.summary: Small town known across Uzbekistan for its handmade knives (pichoq) and black-and-white embroidered skullcaps. Visit a knife workshop and the bazaar.
facts: Knife workshops sell direct; check airline rules before buying
About 45 minutes from Namangan
Market liveliest in the morning

places.name: Samarkand
places.summary: Timur's capital and the most famous Silk Road city, with turquoise domes and tiled madrasas on a monumental scale around the Registan. Needs at least two full days.
facts: Afrosiyob train from Tashkent ~2 h 10 min; book on the Uzbekistan Railways site/app
Most sights have separate tickets; carry cash
Modest dress in mosques and shrines; photo fees at some sites
places.season: Very hot in July–August; April–May and September–October are best.

places.name: Registan
places.summary: Samarkand's great square framed by three tiled madrasas – Ulugh Beg, Sher-Dor and Tilya-Kori with its gilded mosque. One of the great architectural ensembles of the Islamic world.
facts: Ticket ~75,000 UZS for foreigners (approx.)
Return after dark when the square is lit; evening sound-and-light shows on some nights
Early morning has the softest light and fewest people

places.name: Gur-e-Amir Mausoleum
places.summary: Ribbed blue-domed tomb of Timur and his descendants, including Ulugh Beg, with a dazzling gold-and-blue interior. The model for later Mughal tombs like the Taj Mahal.
facts: Ticket ~50,000 UZS (approx.)
Also beautiful lit up in the evening
10 minutes' walk from the Registan

places.name: Bibi-Khanym Mosque
places.summary: Timur's colossal congregational mosque, built after his Indian campaign, once among the largest in the world. Partly rebuilt, its huge portal and domes still overwhelm.
facts: Ticket ~40,000 UZS (approx.)
Right next to Siab Bazaar
Pedestrian street from the Registan leads here

places.name: Siab Bazaar
places.summary: Samarkand's main market beside Bibi-Khanym, piled with dried fruit, nuts, halva and the city's famous round, stamped bread. Great for picnic supplies and tasting.
facts: Free; best in the morning
Closed one day a week (often Monday) – check locally
Samarkand bread keeps for days – good for train journeys

places.name: Shah-i-Zinda
places.summary: Narrow avenue of richly tiled 11th–15th-century mausoleums climbing a hill, around the shrine of Kusam ibn Abbas, cousin of the Prophet. The finest tilework in Samarkand.
facts: Ticket ~40,000–50,000 UZS (approx.)
Go early morning or late afternoon for light and fewer groups
Active pilgrimage site – modest dress and quiet behaviour

places.name: Hazrat Khizr Mosque
places.summary: 19th-century mosque with a carved wooden porch on a hill between Siab Bazaar and Shah-i-Zinda, with a view of Bibi-Khanym. Also holds the mausoleum of Uzbekistan's first president, Islam Karimov, nearby.
facts: Small fee
On the way from the bazaar to Shah-i-Zinda
Good viewpoint over Bibi-Khanym at sunset

places.name: Afrasiyab Museum and ancient city
places.summary: Museum on the grassy mound of ancient Samarkand, destroyed by Genghis Khan in 1220. Its highlight is the 7th-century Sogdian 'Ambassadors' painting showing foreign envoys at the king's court.
facts: Ticket ~40,000 UZS (approx.)
Combine with the Ulugh Beg Observatory 2 km away
The mound itself is mostly unexcavated earthworks

places.name: Ulugh Beg Observatory
places.summary: Remains of the 15th-century observatory of astronomer-ruler Ulugh Beg: the underground arc of a giant meridian sextant and a small museum. A reminder of Samarkand's scientific golden age.
facts: Ticket ~40,000 UZS (approx.)
Small site – 30–45 minutes
On the hill north-east of the old city

places.name: Mausoleum of Khoja Daniyar
places.summary: Long, low shrine on the edge of Afrasiyab above the Siab stream, said to hold the remains of the Prophet Daniel, with an 18 m sarcophagus. Revered by Muslims, Christians and Jews; a peaceful spot with a holy spring.
facts: Free or small fee
Modest dress; women cover hair
Near the Afrasiyab Museum

places.name: Rukhobod Mausoleum
places.summary: Plain 14th-century brick mausoleum near Gur-e-Amir, one of the oldest buildings in the city, built over the tomb of a Sufi mystic. Now houses craft stalls.
facts: Free
2 minutes from Gur-e-Amir
Quick stop

places.name: Konigil Meros paper mill
places.summary: Village workshop on the Siab stream that revived Samarkand's medieval mulberry-bark paper using water-driven mills. You see the whole papermaking process in a shady garden setting.
facts: Ticket ~30,000–50,000 UZS incl. demonstration (approx.)
15 minutes by taxi from the centre
Shop sells paper, notebooks and ceramics

places.name: Imam al-Bukhari Memorial Complex
places.summary: Large, richly decorated memorial complex over the grave of Imam al-Bukhari, the 9th-century compiler of the most respected hadith collection. A major pilgrimage site, rebuilt on a grand scale in recent years.
facts: Free
About 30–40 minutes north of Samarkand
Strict modest dress; women need a headscarf

places.name: Urgut Bazaar
places.summary: Huge market town in the foothills south-east of Samarkand, best known for its weekend bazaar where old and new suzani embroideries are sold. Nearby is the Chor-Chinor garden with ancient plane trees.
facts: Biggest market on Saturday and Sunday mornings
Bargain hard for suzanis; check stitching and fabric
About 50 minutes from Samarkand

places.name: Shahrisabz
places.summary: Timur's birthplace, a green town south of Samarkand over the Takhtakaracha Pass, with the ruins of his giant Ak-Saray palace and the family mausoleums. Its historic centre is a UNESCO site, though heavily cleared and rebuilt.
facts: Day trip from Samarkand (~2 h each way by car)
Main sights are within a 1.5 km walk
Few hotels; most visitors return to Samarkand

places.name: Ak-Saray Palace
places.summary: Ruined portal of Timur's summer palace, once about 65 m high and still towering at nearly 40 m, with fragments of blue, white and gold tilework. Beside it stands a large statue of Timur.
facts: Free to view; small fee may apply for access
Afternoon light is best for photos
Shade is scarce in summer

places.name: Dorut Tilavat and Kok Gumbaz Mosque
places.summary: Ensemble with Ulugh Beg's blue-domed Kok Gumbaz Friday mosque and the mausoleums of Sheikh Shamsiddin Kulyal and Gumbazi Seyidan. Still an active place of worship.
facts: Small entry fee
Modest dress
Walk 300 m to Dorus-Saodat

places.name: Dorus-Saodat and Tomb of Timur
places.summary: Remains of the dynastic complex Timur built for his family, with the mausoleum of his son Jahangir and, nearby, the underground crypt Timur prepared for himself but was never buried in.
facts: Small entry fee
The crypt is a small underground chamber – ask the caretaker if locked
Combine with Dorut Tilavat

places.name: Takhtakaracha Pass
places.summary: Scenic 1,675 m pass on the mountain road between Samarkand and Shahrisabz, with roadside stalls selling honey, fruit and dried apricots and wide views over the Zarafshan range.
facts: Stop on the way to Shahrisabz
Winding road; slow lorries and occasional winter closures
Cool even in summer
places.caution: The road can close after snow in winter; drivers then use the longer route via Guzar.

places.name: Kitab Geological Reserve
places.summary: Mountain reserve east of Shahrisabz with exposed Palaeozoic rock layers rich in fossils, juniper slopes and gorges. A niche excursion for geology fans and hikers.
facts: Arrange a visit with the reserve or a local agency in advance
Rough road; 4x4 recommended
Bring food and water

places.name: Karshi (Qarshi)
places.summary: Capital of Kashkadarya province, a transit town between Samarkand, Bukhara and the south, with the Odina mosque and an old brick bridge. Useful as a stopover rather than a destination.
facts: Afrosiyob/Sharq trains from Tashkent via Samarkand
Shared taxis to Shahrisabz and Bukhara
Very hot in summer

places.name: Boysun
places.summary: Mountain district on the road to Termez whose traditional culture – songs, rituals, crafts – is on UNESCO's intangible heritage list. Village homestays give a rare look at rural life.
facts: Homestays and guesthouses; arrange through a local agency
Boysun Bahori folk festival in spring
Good break on the long drive Shahrisabz–Termez

places.name: Termez
places.summary: Uzbekistan's southernmost city on the Amu Darya facing Afghanistan, a former Kushan-era Buddhist centre. Its museum and nearby Buddhist and Islamic sites make it rewarding for history lovers.
facts: Flights and overnight trains from Tashkent
Hot; the hottest city in the country in summer
Hire a car or taxi for the scattered sites
places.season: Extremely hot June–August (40 °C+); March–May and October–November are best.

places.name: Termez Archaeological Museum
places.summary: Excellent museum of finds from Surkhandarya: Bactrian and Kushan art, Buddhist sculptures and wall paintings from Fayaz Tepe, Kara Tepe and Dalverzin Tepe. Visit before the sites.
facts: Ticket ~30,000–40,000 UZS (approx.)
Allow 1–1.5 hours
Air-conditioned – good for the midday heat

places.name: Fayaz Tepe
places.summary: 1st–3rd-century Buddhist monastery with a restored stupa under a protective dome, a courtyard and cells. The famous Buddha triad found here is in the Tashkent history museum.
facts: Ticket ~30,000 UZS (approx.)
About 20 minutes from central Termez
Little shade

places.name: Kara Tepe
places.summary: Kushan-era Buddhist cave-and-surface monastery complex on hills near the Afghan border, close to Fayaz Tepe. Excavations are ongoing.
facts: Lies in the border zone – access may require arranging in advance via a local agency
Combine with Fayaz Tepe
Very exposed to sun

places.name: Al-Hakim at-Termizi Mausoleum
places.summary: Shrine of the 9th-century Sufi scholar al-Hakim at-Termizi beside the ruins of Old Termez, with carved terracotta decoration. A major pilgrimage site overlooking the Amu Darya.
facts: Free (donations)
Modest dress; women cover hair
Near Fayaz Tepe

places.name: Sultan Saodat Ensemble
places.summary: Group of 10th–17th-century brick mausoleums of the Termez sayyids lining a courtyard on the eastern edge of the city. Quiet and atmospheric.
facts: Small fee or free
15 minutes from the centre
Modest dress

places.name: Zurmala Stupa
places.summary: Eroded 1st–2nd-century mud-brick tower, the oldest surviving Buddhist stupa in Uzbekistan, standing alone in fields near Termez.
facts: Free
Only viewable from outside
Quick stop if passing

places.name: Kampir Tepe
places.summary: Ruins of a Hellenistic-Kushan river port on the Amu Darya, possibly linked to Alexander the Great's crossing, with excavated streets and walls.
facts: Small fee or free
About 30–40 minutes from Termez
Border-area road – carry your passport

places.name: Dalverzin Tepe
places.summary: Kushan city ruins near Denau where a famous hoard of gold and Buddhist sculptures was found. Mostly earth walls and mounds today.
facts: Free
Near Denau, ~2 h from Termez
For enthusiasts; finds are in the Termez and Tashkent museums

places.name: Nurata
places.summary: Small oasis town at the foot of the Nurata mountains with a holy spring and the remains of a fortress attributed to Alexander the Great. Gateway to the Aydarkul yurt camps and village homestays.
facts: Usually visited en route between Samarkand/Bukhara and the yurt camps
Simple guesthouses only
Very hot in summer

places.name: Chashma Spring complex
places.summary: Pilgrimage complex around a sacred spring full of fish, with a domed mosque and a bathhouse, believed to have formed where a meteorite fell. Popular with local pilgrims.
facts: Free
Modest dress
Next to the fortress hill

places.name: Nur Fortress (Alexander's fortress)
places.summary: Earthen remains of the ancient fortress on a hill above the Chashma spring, traditionally said to have been founded by Alexander the Great. Climb for views over the town and the mountains.
facts: Free
Short, steep walk
Best at sunset

places.name: Aydarkul yurt camp
places.summary: Yurt camps in the Kyzylkum desert north of the Nurata mountains, where you sleep in felt yurts, ride camels and eat plov around a campfire under the stars. A favourite overnight stop between Samarkand and Bukhara.
facts: Book ahead; overnight packages usually include dinner, breakfast and a camel ride
Bring a warm layer – desert nights are cold even in late spring
Combine with a swim at Aydarkul lake
places.season: Best April–June and September–October; very hot in midsummer and cold in winter.

places.name: Yangigazgan desert camps
places.summary: Cluster of tourist yurt camps around the village of Yangigazgan on the desert side of the Nurata mountains. An alternative base for camel rides and stargazing.
facts: Book through an agency or directly
Facilities are basic; shared bathrooms
Nights can be cold

places.name: Kyzylkum camel ride
places.summary: Short camel ride over the sand dunes and scrub of the Kyzylkum ('red sand') desert around the yurt camps, ideally at sunset.
facts: Usually included or bookable at the camps
Sunset or early morning rides are the most pleasant
Wear long trousers

places.name: Aydarkul Lake
places.summary: Large brackish lake formed in the 1970s by floodwater from the Syr Darya, stretching for some 250 km across the desert. Camps drive guests to its sandy shore for a swim and fishing.
facts: About 20–30 minutes' drive from the yurt camps
Bring water shoes, sun protection and drinking water
Mosquitoes in the evening in summer

places.name: Sentob
places.summary: Tajik-speaking mountain village in the Nurata range with stone houses, walnut trees and a stream. Community homestays and hikes to neighbouring villages such as Asraf and Hayat.
facts: Homestays with meals; book ahead
Day hikes between villages, ideally with a local guide
Very little phone coverage
places.season: Pleasant from April to October; spring brings blossom and green slopes.

places.name: Asraf
places.summary: Remote village in a narrow valley east of Sentob with terraced orchards and a waterfall, reached on a classic village-to-village hike. Homestays available.
facts: Hike from Sentob takes most of a day
Homestays offer simple rooms and home cooking
Bring cash

places.name: Sarmishsay petroglyphs
places.summary: Gorge in the Karatau hills north-east of Navoi with thousands of rock carvings from the Stone Age to the Middle Ages – hunters, animals and solar symbols.
facts: Free; go with a guide or knowledgeable driver to find the best panels
About 45 minutes from Navoi
Shadeless rocky terrain; carry water

places.name: Navoi
places.summary: Modern industrial city on the Samarkand–Bukhara railway, useful as a stopover and base for Sarmishsay, Rabati Malik and Nurata.
facts: Afrosiyob/Sharq trains stop here
Hotels and taxis available
Few sights of its own

places.name: Bukhara
places.summary: Holy city of Central Asia and the most intact Silk Road town, its lanes, domed bazaars, mosques and madrasas centred on the Lyabi-hauz pool. Easily the most atmospheric place to stay; allow two or three days.
facts: Afrosiyob train from Tashkent ~4 h, from Samarkand ~1.5 h; the station is in Kagan, 15 km away
The old centre is compact and walkable
Modest dress in mosques; some sites charge photo fees
places.season: Very hot June–August; April–May and September–October are ideal.

places.name: Lyabi-hauz Ensemble
places.summary: Shaded pool ringed by mulberry trees, teahouses and the Nadir Divan-Beghi and Kukeldash madrasas – the social heart of old Bukhara. Lovely in the evening.
facts: Free to wander; madrasas host craft shops
Folk show with dinner in Nadir Divan-Beghi in season
Nasreddin Hodja statue is a favourite photo stop

places.name: Po-i-Kalyan (Kalyan Minaret and Mosque)
places.summary: Bukhara's iconic ensemble: the 47 m Kalyan Minaret of 1127, spared by Genghis Khan, the vast Kalyan Mosque and the working Mir-i-Arab Madrasa facing it. Superb at sunset and lit at night.
facts: Kalyan Mosque ticket ~20,000–30,000 UZS (approx.); Mir-i-Arab is viewed from the entrance only
Minaret is not open for climbing
Visit at golden hour and again after dark

places.name: Ark of Bukhara
places.summary: Massive earthen citadel of the emirs of Bukhara, inhabited for more than a millennium, with a ramped gateway, throne room, mosque and small museums. Its walls dominate the Registan square.
facts: Ticket ~60,000 UZS (approx.)
Allow 1–1.5 hours
Opposite the Bolo Hauz Mosque

places.name: Bolo Hauz Mosque
places.summary: Emir's Friday mosque of 1712 facing the Ark, famous for its iwan of tall carved wooden columns reflected in a pool.
facts: Free outside prayer times
Modest dress
Most photogenic in the late afternoon

places.name: Samanid Mausoleum
places.summary: 10th-century brick tomb of the Samanid dynasty in a park west of the Ark, with intricate basket-weave brickwork. One of the masterpieces of early Islamic architecture.
facts: Small ticket (~20,000 UZS, approx.)
Light changes the brick patterns – late afternoon is best
In Samanid Park, next to Chashma-Ayub

places.name: Chashma-Ayub Mausoleum
places.summary: Shrine over a spring said to have been struck by the prophet Job, with an unusual conical dome; inside is a small museum of water supply in Bukhara.
facts: Small ticket
Next to the Samanid Mausoleum
Bukhara Siege Memorial and bazaar nearby

places.name: Magoki-Attori Mosque
places.summary: Bukhara's oldest surviving mosque, sunk below today's street level, with a 12th-century carved facade over earlier foundations. Now a carpet museum.
facts: Small ticket for the carpet museum
Between Lyabi-hauz and the trading domes
Look for the layers of the old city around it

places.name: Trading domes (Toqi)
places.summary: 16th-century domed bazaars at old crossroads – Toqi Sarrofon (money changers), Toqi Telpak Furushon (hats) and Toqi Zargaron (jewellers) – still full of craft and souvenir stalls.
facts: Free; shops open roughly 09:00 to dusk
Bargain politely; compare prices for suzanis and knives
Look for blacksmith and miniature-painting workshops nearby

places.name: Ulugbek and Abdulaziz Khan Madrasas
places.summary: Facing pair of madrasas: Ulugh Beg's 1417 school, the oldest in Central Asia, and the more flamboyant 17th-century Abdulaziz Khan Madrasa with rare figurative tilework.
facts: Small ticket (~20,000 UZS each, approx.)
Next to Toqi Zargaron
Craft shops inside

places.name: Chor Minor
places.summary: Quirky 1807 gatehouse with four turquoise-domed minarets, tucked into a residential lane east of Lyabi-hauz. Climb to the roof for a close look.
facts: Small fee to go up
10 minutes' walk from Lyabi-hauz
Best in morning light

places.name: Sitorai Mokhi-Khosa Palace
places.summary: Summer palace of the last emir of Bukhara, a curious mix of Russian and Uzbek styles with a mirrored White Hall, harem pavilion and gardens with peacocks.
facts: Ticket ~40,000 UZS (approx.)
About 15 minutes north of the centre by taxi
Allow 1–1.5 hours

places.name: Bahauddin Naqshband Complex
places.summary: Memorial complex of the founder of the Naqshbandi Sufi order, Central Asia's most important pilgrimage site, with courtyards, mosques and a sacred tree. Lively on Fridays and holidays.
facts: Free
About 20 minutes east of Bukhara
Modest dress; women cover their hair

places.name: Chor-Bakr Necropolis
places.summary: Walled 'city of the dead' west of Bukhara, a necropolis of the Juybari sheikhs with a mosque, khanaka and lanes of family tombs. Peaceful and seldom crowded.
facts: Ticket ~20,000–30,000 UZS (approx.)
About 15 minutes by taxi
Combine with the Samanid Mausoleum

places.name: Gijduvan
places.summary: Market town north-east of Bukhara, famous for its ceramics with warm brown, yellow and green glazes and for Gijduvan-style shashlik. Has a 15th-century Ulugh Beg madrasa.
facts: On the road from Bukhara towards Nurata/Samarkand
Try the local kebab restaurants
About 50 minutes from Bukhara

places.name: Narzullaev Ceramics Workshop
places.summary: Family ceramics workshop and museum in Gijduvan run by a dynasty of master potters, where you can watch wheel-throwing and glazing and buy pieces.
facts: Free visit; pieces for sale
Call ahead for a demonstration
Pieces are well packed for travel

places.name: Vobkent Minaret
places.summary: Slender 39 m brick minaret of 1196 in the small town of Vobkent, decorated with bands of patterned brickwork and inscriptions.
facts: Free to view from outside
On the road to Gijduvan, 35 minutes from Bukhara
Quick photo stop

places.name: Rabati Malik Caravanserai
places.summary: Monumental portal of an 11th-century royal caravanserai on the Samarkand–Bukhara road, with a restored domed sardoba (water cistern) across the road.
facts: Small fee
Roadside stop between Navoi and Bukhara
Little shade

places.name: Khiva (Itchan Kala)
places.summary: Perfectly preserved walled inner town of the Khiva khanate, packed with madrasas, minarets, palaces and mosques, a UNESCO site that feels like an open-air museum. Magical at sunrise and after dark.
facts: One combined ticket (~200,000 UZS, approx., valid 2 days) covers most museums; some extras charged separately
Stay inside or just outside the walls to enjoy it early and late
Modest dress in mosques and shrines
places.season: Very hot June–August, freezing in January; April–May and September–October are best.

places.name: Kalta Minor
places.summary: Fat, unfinished turquoise-tiled minaret of 1855, intended to be the tallest in the Islamic world but abandoned at 29 m. Khiva's emblem, beside the Mohammed Amin Khan Madrasa.
facts: Viewed from outside; inside the combined-ticket area
Next to the west gate (Ota Darvoza)
Beautiful in early morning

places.name: Kunya-Ark Citadel
places.summary: The khans' fortress-residence inside the west gate, with a tiled summer mosque, throne room and mint. Its Ak Sheikh Bobo bastion is the classic sunset viewpoint over Khiva's domes and minarets.
facts: Included in the combined ticket; the watchtower costs extra (~20,000–30,000 UZS, approx.)
Go up the watchtower an hour before sunset
About 1 hour

places.name: Juma Mosque
places.summary: Unusual hypostyle mosque whose dim hall is supported by 218 carved wooden columns, some dating back to the 10th–11th centuries.
facts: Included in the combined ticket; minaret climb extra
Best when the sun shines through the skylights
About 30 minutes

places.name: Islam Khoja Minaret and Madrasa
places.summary: Khiva's tallest minaret (about 57 m), built in 1910 with bands of turquoise tiles, beside a small madrasa that houses an applied-arts museum. The climb gives the best view of the town.
facts: Minaret climb extra (~20,000–30,000 UZS, approx.)
Steep, dark, narrow stairs
Museum included in the combined ticket

places.name: Tash Hauli Palace
places.summary: Allakuli Khan's 1830s palace with a harem courtyard of tall carved wooden columns and walls of exquisite blue-and-white majolica tiles. The finest interiors in Khiva.
facts: Included in the combined ticket
About 1 hour
Near the east gate

places.name: Pahlavon Mahmud Mausoleum
places.summary: Shrine of Khiva's patron saint, a 14th-century poet, furrier and wrestler, with a turquoise dome and some of the most beautiful tilework in the city. Local couples come here to be blessed.
facts: Separate small ticket may apply
Modest dress; it is a place of pilgrimage
Quieter in the early morning

places.name: Allakuli Khan Madrasa, Caravanserai and Bazaar
places.summary: Group of 19th-century buildings by the east gate (Palvan Darvoza): a madrasa, a caravanserai and a covered bazaar that still leads to the busy farmers' market outside the walls.
facts: Free to walk through the bazaar
Market outside the east gate is liveliest in the morning
Good place to try Khorezmian shivit oshi (green dill noodles) nearby

places.name: Nurullabay Palace
places.summary: Early-20th-century palace in the outer town (Dishan Kala), mixing Khorezmian woodwork and tiles with European stoves, chandeliers and Russian-made ceramics.
facts: Separate ticket (~25,000–50,000 UZS, approx.) or included in some combined tickets
5 minutes' walk north of the west gate
About 45 minutes

places.name: Urgench
places.summary: Modern regional capital of Khorezm with the airport and main railway station for Khiva, 35 km away. A practical base with a few big hotels but little to see.
facts: Taxi to Khiva ~30–40 min; a trolleybus line also links the two
Gateway for the desert fortresses across the Amu Darya
Flights to Tashkent several times a day

places.name: Ayaz Kala
places.summary: The most spectacular of the Khorezm desert fortresses: mud-brick citadels on hilltops above the Kyzylkum, dating from the 4th century BC to the 7th century AD. A yurt camp below lets you stay overnight.
facts: Free or small fee; climbing to the upper fort takes 15–20 minutes
Yurt camp offers dinner and overnight stays – book ahead
Sunset and sunrise are the best times
places.caution: Steep sandy paths and crumbling walls – stay off the ramparts' edges.

places.name: Toprak Kala
places.summary: Rectangular walled city and palace complex of the Khorezmian kings from the 1st–4th centuries AD, with high towers and excavated halls.
facts: Small fee
Combine with Kyzyl Kala nearby (6 km)
No shade; bring water and a hat

places.name: Kyzyl Kala
places.summary: Compact square fortress of red mud-brick, partly restored, standing alone in fields on the road between the Amu Darya and Toprak Kala.
facts: Free or small fee
Quick stop between Toprak Kala and Urgench
Restored walls give a sense of the original look

places.name: Guldursun Kala
places.summary: Large ruined fortress with crumbling towers, wrapped in a legend of a princess who betrayed the city to the Mongols. Closest of the desert fortresses to Urgench and Khiva.
facts: Free
Can be combined with Toprak and Ayaz Kala in a half-day loop
Very exposed – avoid midday in summer

places.name: Nukus
places.summary: Capital of Karakalpakstan, a low Soviet-built city visited mainly for the Savitsky Museum and as the starting point for trips to Moynaq and the Aral Sea.
facts: Flights to Tashkent; trains towards Tashkent and Khiva
Arrange 4x4 trips to the Aral Sea here
Hotels are limited but adequate

places.name: Savitsky Museum (Nukus Museum of Art)
places.summary: Extraordinary collection of banned Soviet avant-garde art rescued by Igor Savitsky, plus Karakalpak jewellery, textiles and Khorezmian archaeology. One of the most important art museums in the former USSR.
facts: Ticket ~50,000 UZS (approx.); photo permit extra
Allow 2–3 hours; guided tours in English are worth booking
Only part of the collection is shown at a time

places.name: Mizdakhan Necropolis
places.summary: Vast hilltop necropolis near Khodjeyli used for over two thousand years, with domed mausoleums, the legendary tomb of Adam and the ruins of the Gyaur Kala fortress.
facts: Free or small fee
About 25 minutes from Nukus
Pilgrims stack bricks for wishes at the Mazlumkhan Sulu crypt – respect the customs

places.name: Chilpik
places.summary: Round mud-brick Zoroastrian dakhma (tower of silence) on a lone hill beside the Amu Darya, where bodies were once exposed to vultures.
facts: Free
Right on the Nukus–Urgench road (~43 km from Nukus)
10-minute climb on loose ground

places.name: Moynaq
places.summary: Former Aral Sea fishing port now more than 100 km from the water, with a small museum about the disaster. A sobering, unforgettable stop.
facts: About 3 hours from Nukus by road
Stihia electronic music festival takes place here some years
A few guesthouses and a hotel

places.name: Moynaq ship cemetery
places.summary: Rusting fishing boats stranded on the sands of the former seabed below the old shoreline, the most powerful symbol of the Aral Sea catastrophe. A memorial and museum stand on the cliff above.
facts: Free; small fee for the museum
Best at sunset
Wear sturdy shoes; metal edges are sharp

places.name: Aral Sea shore (Ustyurt camps)
places.summary: The remaining western basin of the Aral Sea below the cliffs of the Ustyurt plateau, reached by 4x4 across the dried seabed, with yurt camps for an overnight stay. Desolate and moving.
facts: Only by organised 4x4 tour, usually 2 days from Nukus or Moynaq
Bring cash, warm clothes and wet wipes; very basic facilities
Very salty water – you float easily
places.caution: Remote off-road trip with no phone signal for long stretches; go only with an experienced operator.

places.name: Sudochye Lake
places.summary: Wetland system in the old Amu Darya delta near Moynaq, an important stopover for migrating birds, with an abandoned fishing village on its shore.
facts: Reached by rough tracks; usually visited on Aral Sea tours
Best for birds in spring and autumn
Bring insect repellent

places.name: Tashkent Airport (TAS)
places.summary: Uzbekistan's main airport, inside the city: 20–30 min to the centre by taxi (Yandex Go).
facts: Many flights from Europe land at night or early morning
SIM cards (Ucell, Beeline, Uzmobile) are sold in arrivals; bring your passport
Domestic flights leave from the separate domestic terminal: check which one

places.name: Samarkand Airport (SKD)
places.summary: Samarkand's airport, 15 min from the Registan, with some direct flights from Europe and Istanbul.
facts: Open-jaw tickets (into Samarkand, home from Tashkent) save a day

places.name: Bukhara Airport (BHK)
places.summary: Bukhara's airport, 15 min from the old town.
facts: Flights to Tashkent and Moscow; a few to Istanbul

places.name: Urgench Airport (UGC)
places.summary: The airport for Khiva: 35–40 min by taxi to the Itchan Kala.
facts: Flights to Tashkent take about 1 h 40 min
Taxis to Khiva wait outside arrivals; agree the price first

places.name: Nukus Airport (NCU)
places.summary: Nukus's small airport, 10 min from the Savitsky Museum.
facts: Flights to Tashkent

places.name: Termez Airport (TMJ)
places.summary: Termez's airport, 15 min from town.
facts: Flights to Tashkent take about 1 h 30 min

bookings.note: Tashkent (TAS); open-jaw via Samarkand or Urgench saves backtracking.
Tashkent → Samarkand → Bukhara, per person. Book on eticket.railway.uz.
Or the train from Bukhara (6–7 h).
Shahrisabz, the Khorezm fortresses, Nurata: a driver for the day.
Per person, with dinner and breakfast.
Registan, Shah-i-Zinda, Ark, Itchan Kala and the rest.

links.name: Uzbekistan Railways tickets
links.note: Afrosiyob and other trains. Seats go on sale about 45 days ahead and sell out: book early.

links.name: Uzbekistan Airways
links.note: Domestic flights: Tashkent ↔ Urgench, Nukus, Termez, Bukhara.

links.name: Uzbekistan e-visa
links.note: Many nationalities (including the EU) need no visa for up to 30 days; others apply here.

links.name: Uzbekistan Travel (tourism board)
links.note: Official tourism site: sights, festivals and practical information.

checklist: Passport valid 3+ months after you leave. EU citizens: no visa for up to 30 days; check the rule for your nationality.
Registration: hotels and guesthouses register you with the authorities. Keep the slips; you may be asked for them when you leave.
Book train tickets early (eticket.railway.uz): the Afrosiyob between Tashkent, Samarkand and Bukhara sells out days ahead.
Cash: bring euros or dollars in clean, recent notes to change at banks. Cards work in bigger hotels and in Tashkent.
Dress modestly in mosques and madrasas: shoulders and knees covered; women carry a scarf. Shoes off where asked.
Summer (June–August) is 40 °C+ in Bukhara and Khiva: sightsee early and late. Spring and autumn are the best seasons.
Medicines: some common ones (codeine, some sleeping pills) are controlled. Bring prescriptions in the original packs.
Drones need a permit and are confiscated at the border without one.
Some sites charge a separate photo or video fee; the Itchan Kala in Khiva has one combined ticket.
